attack_mechanism: For a load or store issued while `mstatus_mprv = 1`, the control unit assigns `ctrl_o.lsu_priv <= csr.mstatus_mpp`. `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.dpc` can alter the CSR write, trap/debug return, or stored `mstatus_mpp` value used by that MPRV branch; the transfer is guarded in the RTL by `neorv32_cpu.dbus_req.meta`, `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.alu_opa_mux`, `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.alu_sub`, `neorv32_cpu_control.branch_taken`, and the remaining path guards. By manipulating `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.dpc` before the CSR/control state is committed, an attacker can select or program the more privileged branch for a chosen load/store. The operative RTL path is `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.dpc -> neorv32_cpu_control.exec_nxt.pc2 -> neorv32_cpu.alu_add -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. The LSU request metadata carries an unintended effective privilege, allowing a memory access to be checked as a more privileged operation.

The assignment `lsu_priv <= mstatus_mpp when mstatus_mprv = '1' else prv_level` makes `mstatus_mprv` the privilege-source selector. `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.dpc` reaches that selector or one of its CSR update controls; the transfer is guarded in the RTL by `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.csr_re`, `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.csr_we`, `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv`. By manipulating `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.dpc` before the CSR/control state is committed, an attacker can select or program the more privileged branch for a chosen load/store. The operative RTL path is `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.dpc -> neorv32_cpu.csr_rdata -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr_wdata -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. The LSU selects the wrong privilege source and applies an unintended protection domain to the pending memory request.
